expected_events.summary: ACTOM is expanding manufacturing at its Pretoria West facility, which has been transformed into an integrated energy-equipment hub. Its approximately R40 million investment is creating approximately 80 employment opportunities; the article does not establish that all those roles have been filled.
quotes: ACTOM’s continued expansion of its manufacturing operations at its Pretoria West facility

The revitalised Pretoria West facility has been transformed into an integrated manufacturing hub for large power transformers, high-voltage equipment and lithium-ion battery energy storage systems, strengthening South Africa’s capability to manufacture critical energy infrastructure locally while supporting industrial growth, job creation and export competitiveness.

ACTOM’s aggregate consolidated investment of approximately R40 million across its High Voltage Equipment and Static Energy operations reflects the Group’s long-term commitment to local manufacturing and industrial expansion, while creating approximately 80 new employment opportunities and strengthening South Africa’s strategic energy manufacturing capability

expected_events.summary: Rentoza entered voluntary business rescue on 1 July 2026 and remains in operation while a practitioner develops its restructuring plan; this is not a confirmed closure.
quotes: South African technology subscription platform Rentoza announced that it entered voluntary business rescue on 1 July 2026, saying the company will continue operating while a restructuring plan is developed.

expected_events.summary: Rentoza secured R20 million from the Mineworkers Investment Company in 2022, helping expand its subscription platform across South Africa.
quotes: In 2022, the startup secured R20 million in funding from the Mineworkers Investment Company, capital that helped expand its subscription platform across South Africa.
Rentoza built its reputation by allowing consumers to subscribe to smartphones, laptops, gaming consoles, household appliances, fitness equipment and other products instead of buying them outright.

expected_events.summary: Vodacom South Africa is restructuring and consulting over retrenchments. The company says circa 113 employees could be affected, while the report says 400 workers were consulted; neither figure establishes completed layoffs in this round. The report is dated 26 February 2025.
quotes: According to the source, Vodacom this week made a presentation to the employees about its plans to initiate a Section 189 retrenchment process.

Vodacom South Africa has taken the difficult decision to restructure parts of our business, which unfortunately could impact circa 113 of our valued employees, across various levels, including management and senior management
While Vodacom says 113 employees will be impacted, ITWeb understands that 400 workers have been consulted about the Section 189 process.

expected_events.summary: In an earlier round, described as March last year in the February 2025 report, Vodacom introduced an operational review and cost-cutting process that affected at least 80 jobs.
quotes: This is not the first time Vodacom has wielded the axe on its employees.

In March last year, the company [introduced](https://www.itweb.co.za/article/vodacom-sa-employees-face-retrenchments/VgZey7JleeEqdjX9) an operational review and cost-cutting process that impacted a minimum of 80 jobs.
V

expected_events.summary: An earlier merger, approved in January 2021, gave Stanlib Fund II joint control of Solar Capital De Aar 3. The notice confirms the acquiring group already jointly controls the target through that previous merger.
quotes: In January 2021, the Tribunal unconditionally approved the large merger whereby Greenstreet 1 (Pty) Ltd (“Stanlib Fund II”) sought to acquire a joint controlling interest in Solar Capital De Aar 3 (RF) (Pty) Ltd (“SCDA 3”).

Through the previous merger, the acquiring group jointly controls the target firm, SCDA 3, which is active within the renewable energy sector as an IPP contracted under the REIPPPP to supply solar PV to Eskom.
relevant markets in South Africa

expected_events.summary: The notice dated 2021-03-02 reports unconditional approval for a further acquisition of SCDA 3 shares that will give Stanlib Fund II sole control. Completion of this further transaction is not established.
quotes: Subsequent to that merger, the Tribunal has also unconditionally approved the transaction whereby Stanlib Fund II will acquire additional shareholding in SCDA 3. Post-transaction, Stanlib Fund II will hold a sole controlling interest in SCDA 3.
relevant markets in South Africa

expected_events.summary: The notice dated 2021-03-02 reports unconditional approval for Aker Horizons to acquire sole control of Mainstream Renewable Power. The transaction will establish Aker Horizons in South Africa; its parent’s existing presence is distinct.
quotes: Following the unconditional approval of this transaction by the Tribunal, Aker Horizons AS (“Aker”) will acquire sole control of Mainstream Renewable Power Ltd (“MRP”).
Aker does not have a presence in South Africa and the transaction will establish Aker’s entry into the country.

expected_events.summary: Isuzu launched its South African business operations following acquisitions of the Port Elizabeth light-commercial-vehicle operation and remaining shares in Isuzu Trucks South Africa. The manufacturing operation is described as wholly owned.
quotes: Isuzu Motors has launched its business operations in South Africa.  This follows the announcement of last year where Isuzu had said that it would purchase the light commercial vehicle operations in Port Elizabeth and also the balance of shareholding in its Isuzu Trucks South Africa operations.
manufacturing plant in Struandale Port Elizabeth
This is the first commercial and light commercial vehicle manufacturing operation outside of Japan in which we have acquired a 100% ownership.

expected_events.summary: Isuzu had acquired a 57.7% majority stake in a Kenyan truck and bus assembly operation a year before the report. The supplied evidence does not establish an absolute acquisition date.
quotes: Isuzu is making positive strides in Africa and a year ago the company acquired a 57.7% majority shareholding in the Kenyan truck and bus assembly operation which supplies Isuzu vehicles to East African markets, while commanding a leading 34% share of the Kenyan new vehicle market.

expected_events.summary: As part of post-acquisition consolidation, Isuzu Motors South Africa set out a short-term plan to relocate truck operations from Kempston Road to the Struandale plant in Port Elizabeth. Completion of the relocation is not stated.
quotes: Isuzu Motors South Africa CEO and MD Michael Sacke said that the company's initial focus would be to fully consolidate its operations while laying the foundation for the company's future success.

Our short-term focus is on implementing our transitional plans, ensuring the sustainability of our operations, further strengthening our product portfolio and relocating the truck operations from Kempston Road to the Struandale plant.
manufacturing plant in Struandale Port Elizabeth

expected_events.summary: Telkom was considering moving its head office from downtown Pretoria to its Highveld campus in Centurion. The report explicitly says nothing was confirmed and no final decision on a possible move would be taken before its property review was complete.
quotes: Telkom is giving serious thought to relocating its head office from downtown Pretoria to facilities closer to Johannesburg — at its campus in Highveld in Centurion — in a move designed mainly to cut costs
Nothing is confirmed at this stage, but it’s understood the move, if it happens, could save the company as much as R200m/year.
no final decisions will be taken regarding the nature and timing of any possible moves until the review has been completed.

expected_events.summary: Telkom had already moved some head-office functions to its Centurion campus. This completed partial move is distinct from the unconfirmed proposal to move the whole head office.
